ADR-001: Four layers of record, each with a test for what belongs in it
ADR-002: Contributions write fragments; shared documents are generated views
ADR-003: Status is a closed vocabulary in frontmatter, enforced by lint
ADR-004: The decision index is generated from frontmatter
ADR-005: References in prose are hyperlinks, enforced by lint
ADR-006: Reference schemes and paths are configuration, not constants
ADR-007: Document status is reported, not enforced
ADR-008: One directive vocabulary, one scope rule
ADR-009: Extracted with provenance, not imported
ADR-010: Name the project `chester`, after Chesterton's Fence
ADR-011: Name the project Luria, after *The Mind of a Mnemonist*
ADR-012: Principles are fragments too, rendered as a document
ADR-013: A document's filename is its code; the title lives in the frontmatter
ADR-014: A code that resolves to nothing is reported, not dropped
ADR-015: A foreign record gets a prefix; the config turns it into a URL
ADR-016: Remotes are public URLs, Luria is its own worked example, and every scheme versions
ADR-017: A reference may name a document before its URL resolves
ADR-018: The README's badges are counts derived from the record
ADR-019: A wrong reason is corrected in place and versioned; a changed choice is superseded
ADR-020: The devlog is a journal: dated entries that persist, rendered into books
ADR-021: The read/write boundary: views in docs/, sources in record/
ADR-022: `url-ok` acknowledges foreign codes only
ADR-023: A remote constructs per scheme: dir, document + anchor, or url
ADR-024: A remote reference is a prefix, a delimiter and a uid — numbers are the special case
ADR-025: Wikilinks: `[[CODE]]` is a typed reference, and typing it changes the rules
ADR-026: One ordered pmap over threads; width is an environment variable
ADR-027: Published to PyPI via trusted publishing; the scaffold ships inside the package
ADR-028: Collection styles are configuration; the changelog shape is one of them
ADR-029: A generated view must be committed by something; the remedy says so where it is read
ADR-030: The CLI surface is the workflows, not the module layout
ADR-031: A fact the tree already states is populated, not demanded
ADR-032: The status reports are committed views, and the badges land on them
ADR-033: A document can opt out of reference checking, and the report counts it
ADR-034: Fixture codes come from a registered prefix, not from the sequence
ADR-035: Status enforcement is a dial — reported by default, failable by configuration
ADR-036: One scaffold for every entry kind — `luria new`, driven by the config
ADR-037: The agent file is a map, not a copy
ADR-038: The CLI is the interface; the Makefile retires
ADR-039: Drive the CLI with Fire: typed functions, derived flags
ADR-040: Migrations: renaming schemes and moving documents without losing the record's memory
ADR-041: Bugs enter the record characterized: the minimal working example protocol
ADR-042: The record publishes as a Quartz vault: paths preserved, sources withheld, frontmatter surfaced
ADR-043: The site wears the project's brand: artwork by path, favicon rasterized at build time
ADR-044: The configuration reference is generated from the config schema
ADR-045: Worked configurations are executable examples, not prose
ADR-046: Reference detection is scheme-driven, not three hardcoded patterns
ADR-047: A declared family replaces the default; settings still merge
ADR-048: The scaffold is planned from configuration, not copied from a tree
ADR-049: Temporary codes at filing; concretized and aliased at the serialization point
ADR-050: Titles in a transferable scheme are checked against the project's own nouns
ADR-051: Prose frontmatter is what the generator renders, not what the author prefers
ADR-052: The draft signal: a contribution that asks for a verdict, not a review
ADR-053: The published version is derived from the release tag
ADR-054: A scheme can constrain which of its tags combine
ADR-055: A link target is checked from where the prose renders
ADR-056: A scheme declares which statuses it uses and what they mean
ADR-057: A scheme whose status never varies is reported
ADR-058: Luria is a truth maintenance system, and should say so
ADR-059: The configuration reference renders where its schema lives; every project gets its own record description
ADR-060: Schemes declare their own shape — where the vocabulary lives, and what a field means
ADR-061: A scheme's template is a form, not a document
ADR-062: A suppressed build is branch protection's problem, not the lint's
ADR-063: Init takes shorthand and writes ordinary tables
ADR-064: Files are UTF-8; the console is the platform's
ADR-065: A principle is written as a value, unless it is actually a rule
ADR-066: Remote content endorsed by hash, drift compared offline
ADR-067: A code relates to named URIs through one template vocabulary
ADR-068: Source repairs are committed on the branch that authored them; generated views on the default branch only
ADR-069: A workflow file cites decisions in a form the generation job's token can commit: by number, or in prose
ADR-070: A decision is stated for what it chooses; a prohibition is reserved for a constraint that has been verified
ADR-071: Typed edges come from fields, and a superseded document names its successor in `superseded_by:`
ADR-072: The status note is its own field
ADR-073: A finding names the key that declared its obligation; the record page lists the contract; no explain verb
ADR-074: A scheme can require one of several fields
ADR-075: A reference field declares whether it holds one code or many; a list where one was declared is a finding
ADR-076: A frontmatter field can be backed by a scheme-local controlled vocabulary
ADR-077: Publish a nested record as a section of its parent site, staged by its own config
ADR-078: A nested record's views are generated and committed with the parent's
ADR-079: Read a note's frontmatter comments as directive comments
ADR-080: A remote declares how to ask what an identifier is, and the lint may ask
ADR-081: `inert-status` measures a distribution, and its threshold is the project's to set
ADR-082: A field can be required by another field's value
ADR-083: A relation is walked transitively and rendered as sequences, on one page
ADR-084: A relation declares its converse; symmetry is the self-converse case
ADR-085: Status is an ordinary controlled vocabulary; a built-in is a declaration nobody wrote
ADR-086: A marked region is how the README carries a derived fact
ADR-087: Identity is a field; the filename is a projection of it
ADR-088: A derived alias is kept; a former spelling is rewritten
ADR-089: A derived field is read-only, unlike a derived URI
ADR-090: The block below a directive is a syntactic unit, read from a grammar when one is installed
ADR-091: A stack of pull requests lands from the tip
ADR-092: A derivation may follow a reference: one hop, against written frontmatter
ADR-093: Fixture schemes come from a reserved namespace
ADR-tmp0hx52: A project can show a graph it designed in place of Quartz's
ADR-tmp40zph: A document-rendered scheme's sources are published as pages
ADR-tmpronup: A document's typed lineage is drawn on its page, beside Quartz's graph
